newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BAYERN MUNICH V BORUSSIA DORTMUND TACTICS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BAYERN MUNICH V BORUSSIA DORTMUND TACTICS.

text.p: Following is an analysis of the strengths and weaknesses of Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund who clash in Munich in the German first division on Sunday (kickoff 1700 GMT):

Playing style: On the surface, typically German with a libero, two out-and-out defenders at the back and versatile midfielders down the flanks who can defend and attack. But coach Giovanni Trapattoni, one of the great thinkers in the game, adds a few Italian touches to the tactics and Bayern are flexible. Veteran Lothar Matthaeus fills the influential libero role and has been going forward more recently. Mehmet Scholl is one of the playmakers behind strikers Juergen Klinsmann and Alexander Zickler. Midfielder Mario Basler is normally also active down the right flank pushing Bayern forward with his creative running.

Strengths: Despite a few injuries they have more top players fit than Dortmund as well as home advantage. Last weekend Klinsmann ended his recent goalscoring problems and should feel more relaxed. Their early exit from the UEFA Cup has also taken pressure off their fixture programme.

Weaknesses: Bayern's main problem in recent years has been controversy in the dressing rooms. The club has so many leading personalities that there have often been arguments and chairman Franz Beckenbauer has had to step in. It is impossible to predict when the next scandal will hit the club. Bayern can also blow hot and cold. Some days they are brilliant, others calamitous.

Motivation: A capacity crowd in Munich's huge Olympic stadium should provide an incentive. Bayern are unbeaten at home this season winning four of their five games. With nothing to play for on the international scene, they will be keen to put one over on their arch-rivals.

Probable line-up with shirt numbers: 1-Oliver Kahn, 10-Lothar Matthaeus, 2-Markus Babbel, 15-Samuel Kuffour, 13-Mario Basler, 8-Thomas Strunz, 7-Mehmet Scholl, 6-Christian Nerlinger, 3-Markus Muench, 18-Juergen Klinsmann, 21-Alexander Zickler

Playing style: Under normal circumstances Dortmund play a 3-5-2 system with libero Matthias Sammer playing the flexible Franz Beckenbauer role but injuries have forced coach Ottmar Hitzfeld to change his team and tactics almost every week this season. Against Atletico Madrid in the champions' league on Wednesday, Wolfgang Feiersinger came in as libero and Julio Cesar and Juergen Kohler were man-to-man markers. Cesar, Kohler and Rene Schneider can all play libero, however. Hitzfeld may just play Stephane Chapuisat as the only striker with midfielder Lars Ricken and Rene Tretschok just behind on the right and left sides respectively. There is some hope that playmaker Andy Moeller may be fit to return which would add extra edge to their attack.
Strengths: European midweek 1-0 victory in Madrid which effectively puts the team in the quarter-finals of European Cup has boosted morale after some inconsistent form domestically.

Weaknesses: What the Germans call the "English week" of constant midweek and weekend matches has given Dortmund a tough programme recently and they are struggling to make up for their long list of injuries.

Motivation: There is no need to motivate players when they step into Munich's magnificent Olympic stadium -- the venue of the 1974 World Cup final and the 1988 European championship final. Every club wants to beat Bayern -- especially on their home turf.

Dortmund line-up (from) - 1-Stefan Klos, 20-Wolfgang Feiersinger, 5-Julio Cesar, 15-Juergen Kohler, 14-Paul Lambert, 7-Stefan Reuter, 17-Joerg Heinrich, 8-Michael Zorc, 18-Lars Ricken, 10-Andy Moeller, 23-Rene Tretschok, 9-Stephane Chapuisat.
